svg.title: Xen Orchestra attack chain: empty-object cookie to XCP-ng host compromise
svg.text: From an empty cookie to the hypervisor
How the November 2026 Xen Orchestra attacks worked. Source: Vates advisories VSA-2026-062 and VSA-2026-063.

g.text: Send a cookie holding an empty JSON object
authenticationToken=j:{} (or URL-encoded, j:%7B%7D) to the Xen Orchestra REST API. No password needed.
The empty object matches every stored token
The server returns the first one. If it has not expired, the attacker is logged in as that token's owner.
The route /rest/v0/users/me/authentication_tokens hands back token IDs that keep working.
Import a VM with crafted keys to reach the XCP-ng host (VSA-2026-063)
Xen Orchestra forwards VM imports to the hypervisor with pool-admin rights and does not inspect them,
so settings like a serial console pointed at a host file get through.
Steps 1 to 3: CVE-2026-133469, rated 9.8. Fixed in Xen Orchestra 6.9.2 (stable) and 6.10.1 (latest).
Step 4: no fix in either channel at Vates's last update (10 Nov). Remove import and network permissions.
